claim: Federal Constitution Art. 14(1)(b): a person born on or after Malaysia Day (16 Sep 1963) is a citizen by operation of law only if they have one of the qualifications in Part II of the Second Schedule
quote: every person born on or after Malaysia Day, and having any of the qualifications specified in Part II of the Second Schedule.
note: Reprint as at 30 November 2025 (cover page); sources.csv lists page_date as undated

claim: A child born in Malaysia is a citizen by operation of law if at least one parent is, at the time of the birth, a Malaysian citizen or a permanent resident of Malaysia (Second Schedule Part II s.1(a)). A child of two Bangladeshi parents who are neither citizens nor permanent residents does not qualify under this rule
quote: every person born within the Federation of whose parents one at least is at the time of the birth either a citizen or permanently resident in the Federation
note: Second Schedule Part II s.1(a); reprint as at 30 Nov 2025

claim: The only other birth-in-Malaysia route is for a child who is not born a citizen of any country (Second Schedule Part II s.1(e)), and for that rule any citizenship the child acquires within one year after birth (e.g. by consular registration under the parents' country's law) counts as citizenship at birth (s.2(3))
quote: every person born within the Federation who is not born a citizen of any country otherwise than by virtue of this paragraph
note: Second Schedule Part II s.1(e). Whether a child of Bangladeshi parents gets Bangladeshi citizenship by descent depends on Bangladesh law (not in this source)

claim: Second Schedule Part II s.2(3): for the stateless-at-birth rule, a person is treated as having at birth any citizenship acquired within one year afterwards by a provision corresponding to consular registration or otherwise
quote: For the purposes of paragraph (e) of section 1, a person is to be treated as having at birth any citizenship which he acquires within one year afterwards by virtue of any provision corresponding to paragraph (c) of that section or otherwise.
note: Second Schedule Part II s.2(3)

claim: Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1752), not yet in force at the 30 Nov 2025 reprint, will narrow s.1(a): only a citizen parent (not a permanent-resident parent) will give citizenship to a child born in Malaysia
quote: This Part was amended by Act A1752, paragraph 11(a), not yet in force, as follows: Section 1 a. in paragraph (a), the words "a citizen" substituted for the words "either a citizen or permanently resident in the Federation".
note: Need to know: commencement date of Act A1752 after 30 Nov 2025

claim: Decisions of the Federal Government under the citizenship Part of the Constitution cannot be appealed or reviewed in any court
quote: A decision of the Federal Government under Part III of this Constitution shall not be subject to appeal or review in any court.
note: Second Schedule Part III s.2

claim: No non-citizen may enter Malaysia without a valid Entry Permit or a valid Pass lawfully issued to them (or an exemption order); entering without one is an offence punishable by a fine of up to RM10,000 or up to 5 years' prison or both, plus up to 6 strokes of whipping (s.6)
quote: No person other than a citizen shall enter Malaysia unless-- (a) he is in possession of a valid Entry Permit lawfully issued to him under section 10; (b) his name is endorsed upon a valid Entry Permit in accordance with section 12, and he is in the company of the holder of the Permit; (c) he is in possession of a valid Pass lawfully issued to him to enter Malaysia; or (d) he is exempted from this section by an order made under section 55.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.6(1)

claim: Penalty for entering Malaysia without a valid pass or permit: fine up to RM10,000 or prison up to 5 years or both, and up to 6 strokes of whipping (s.6(3)); the person must prove they entered lawfully (s.6(4))
quote: Any person who contravenes subsection (1) shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to both, and shall also be liable to whipping of not more than six strokes.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.6(3)

claim: A non-citizen who cannot show means of supporting themself (and dependants) or definite employment awaiting them, or who is likely to become a pauper or charge on the public, is a prohibited immigrant (s.8(3)(a))
quote: any person who is unable to show that he has the means of supporting himself and his dependants (if any) or that he has definite employment awaiting him, or who is likely to become a pauper or a charge on the public;
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.8(3)(a). The Act does not set an amount of money

claim: Also prohibited immigrants: anyone whose entry was unlawful (s.8(3)(h)); anyone without the travel documents required by law or holding forged or altered travel documents (s.8(3)(m)); and the family and dependants of a prohibited immigrant (s.8(3)(n))
quote: any person who, being required by any written law for the time being in force to be in possession of valid travel documents, is not in possession of those documents or is in possession of forged or altered travel documents or travel documents which do not fully comply with any such written law;
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.8(3)(h),(m),(n)

claim: A permit holder refused entry on arrival as a prohibited immigrant may appeal to the Minister, whose decision is final (s.8(6)); while the appeal is pending they are held in an immigration depot unless released on a pass
quote: any person in possession of a Permit issued to him under this Act who, upon his arrival in Malaysia, is refused permission to enter upon the ground that he is a prohibited immigrant, may appeal against the refusal within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed, to the Minister, whose decision shall be final
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.8(6). Applies to Permit holders; no appeal for those barred under s.8(3)(o)

claim: The Director General of Immigration may by order bar any person or class of persons from entering or re-entering Malaysia for a stated period or permanently (s.9(1)(a)), and may cancel any Pass at any time in his absolute discretion (s.9(1)(b))
quote: prohibit, either for a stated period or permanently, the entry or re-entry into Malaysia of any person or class of persons
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.9(1)

claim: If a person's Pass is cancelled while they are in Malaysia, they must leave, are removed, and are afterwards prohibited from entering Malaysia (s.9(4)(a)); the pass holder can appeal to the Minister in writing within 7 days of notification, but the cancellation applies while the appeal is pending (s.9(8))
quote: if its holder is present in Malaysia, he shall not remain in Malaysia after such cancellation and shall be removed from Malaysia in accordance with the provisions of this Act, and he shall, thereafter, be prohibited from entering Malaysia
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.9(4)(a), s.9(8)

claim: Appeal against an entry ban order or pass cancellation: to the Minister within seven days, by written petition setting out the grounds in detail (s.9(8))
quote: may appeal to the Minister within seven days of the publication of the order in the Gazette under subsection (2), or the notification of the cancellation to the holder of the Pass or Permit under subsection (3), as the case may be, and such appeal shall be by way of a petition in writing setting out clearly and in detail the grounds of the appeal
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.9(8)

claim: Overstaying: a person must not remain in Malaysia after their pass expires or after notice that it has been cancelled (s.15(1)(c),(d)); doing so without reasonable cause is punishable by a fine of not less than RM10,000 or prison up to 5 years or both (s.15(4))
quote: Any person who without reasonable cause contravenes this section shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of not less than ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to both.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.15(4). Note the wording is 'not less than' RM10,000 (a minimum), unlike s.6(3)

claim: s.15(1)(c): a person shall not remain in Malaysia after the expiration of the period of any Pass relating to or issued to him, unless otherwise authorised
quote: after the expiration of the period of any Pass relating to or issued to him
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text, so no newer consolidated text was available; s.15(1)(c)

claim: A person convicted of unlawful entry or of being a prohibited immigrant (offences under s.5, 6, 8 or 9) is liable to be removed from Malaysia by order of the Director General (s.32(1))
quote: Any person who is convicted of an offence under section 5, 6, 8 or 9 shall be liable to be removed from Malaysia by order of the Director General
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.32(1)

claim: A person unlawfully in Malaysia because of an expired or cancelled pass (s.9, 15) is removed by order of the Director General whether or not they are prosecuted (s.33(1))
quote: Where the presence of any person in Malaysia is unlawful by reason of section 9, 15 or 60 the person shall, whether or not any proceedings are taken against him in respect of any offence against this Act, be removed from Malaysia by order of the Director General.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.33(1)

claim: A removal order can normally be appealed to the Minister (s.33(2)), but there is no appeal where the person's presence is unlawful because their pass expired or was cancelled
quote: or is unlawful under paragraph 15(1)(c) or section 60 by reason of the expiry of any Pass relating to or issued to him.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.33(2) and proviso

claim: A person ordered to be removed may be held in custody (prison, police station or immigration depot) for as long as needed to arrange removal (s.34)
quote: such person may be detained in custody for such period as may be necessary for the purpose of making arrangements for his removal
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.34(1),(3)

claim: A person believed liable to removal can be arrested without warrant by an authorised immigration officer or senior police officer and held up to 30 days while removal is decided (s.35)
quote: may be detained in any prison, police station or immigration depot for a period not exceeding thirty days pending a decision as to whether an order for his removal should be made.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.35

claim: Returning to or living in Malaysia unlawfully after being removed is an offence: fine up to RM10,000 or up to 5 years in prison or both, up to 6 strokes of whipping, and removal again (s.36)
quote: Any person who, having been lawfully removed or otherwise sent out of Malaysia, unlawfully enters Malaysia or unlawfully resides in Malaysia shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to both and shall also be liable to whipping of not more than six strokes
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.36

claim: If a person cannot produce their valid pass or permit (or other accepted proof) when an immigration or police officer asks, the court presumes they entered or stayed unlawfully until they prove otherwise (s.56(4))
quote: it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that he has, as the case may be, entered or re-entered or remained in Malaysia unlawfully.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.56(4)

claim: Employing a non-citizen who does not hold a valid Pass is an offence: fine of RM10,000 to RM50,000 or up to 12 months in prison or both, for each such employee (s.55B(1))
quote: Any person who employs one or more persons, other than a citizen or a holder of an Entry Permit who is not in possession of a valid Pass shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of not less than ten thousand ringgit but not more than fifty thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months or to both for each such employee.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.55B(1)

claim: A pass stops being valid as soon as any of its terms and conditions is broken (s.55B(2))
quote: A Pass lawfully issued to any person shall cease to be a valid Pass when any of its terms and conditions is contravened.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.55B(2). The worker-side offence for breaching pass conditions is in the Immigration Regulations 1963 (reg. 39, referred to in s.55E(7)), not in this file

claim: An employer who employed more than five workers without valid passes at the same time faces 6 months to 5 years in prison and up to 6 strokes of whipping (s.55B(3)); anyone doing work normally done by an employee is presumed employed, paid or not (s.55B(4)); company directors and managers are liable too (s.55B(5))
quote: it is proved to the satisfaction of the court that the person has at the same time employed more than five such employees that person shall, on conviction be liable to imprisonment for a term of not less than six months but not more than five years and shall also be liable to whipping of not more than six strokes.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.55B(3)-(5)

claim: Anyone directly or indirectly involved in bringing a person into Malaysia contrary to the Act faces a fine of RM10,000-50,000 and 2-5 years in prison and up to 6 strokes (s.55A(1))
quote: Any person involved, directly or indirectly, in conveying to Malaysia in or on any vehicle, vessel or aircraft any person contrary to this Act shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of not less than ten thousand ringgit but not more than fifty thousand ringgit and to imprisonment for a term of not less than two years but not more than five years and shall also be liable to whipping of not more than six strokes.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.55A(1)

claim: Making, forging or altering an endorsement or document to be used as a visa, permit or pass: fine of RM30,000-100,000 and 5-10 years in prison and up to 6 strokes of whipping (s.55D)
quote: Any person who makes, forges or alters an endorsement or a document to be used as a visa, Permit, Pass or Certificate under this Act shall be guilty of an offence against this Act and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of not less than thirty thousand ringgit but not more than one hundred thousand ringgit and to imprisonment for a term of not less than five years but not more than ten years and shall also be punished with whipping of not more than six strokes.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.55D

claim: A person who has charge of premises (landlord, employer's hostel, etc.) and lets an illegal immigrant enter or stay there: fine RM5,000-30,000 or up to 12 months or both per illegal immigrant (s.55E(2)); 'illegal immigrant' includes anyone breaching s.5, 6, 8, 9 or 15 (e.g. overstayers) or regulation 39 of the Immigration Regulations 1963 (s.55E(7))
quote: illegal immigrant' means a person, other than a citizen, who contravenes section 5, 6, 8, 9 or 15 of this Act or regulation 39 of the Immigration Regulations 1963
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.55E(2),(7)

claim: Offences under s.56(1) include: false report or statement in connection with the Act (f); using a pass issued to someone else (j); getting a pass for oneself or another by a false statement (k); using or possessing a forged, altered or irregular pass or permit (l). Penalty: fine up to RM10,000 or up to 5 years in prison (s.56(1)(aa))
quote: except for an offence under paragraph (d), be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years;
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.56(1)(f),(j),(k),(l),(aa)

claim: s.56(1)(k): obtaining or trying to obtain a pass or permit for oneself or another by making a false statement is an offence
quote: obtains or attempts to obtain for himself or for any other person by making a false statement any Entry Permit, Pass, Internal Travel Document or Certificate
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.56(1)(k)

claim: s.56(1)(l): using, or having without lawful authority, a forged, unlawfully altered or irregular permit or pass is an offence
quote: uses or without lawful authority has in his possession any forged, unlawfully altered or irregular Entry Permit, Pass, Internal Travel Document or Certificate or other document issued under this Act
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.56(1)(l)

claim: Harbouring a person known (or reasonably believed) to have broken the Immigration Act: fine RM10,000-50,000 per person harboured; more than five at once: 6 months-5 years in prison and up to 6 strokes (s.56(1)(d),(bb))
quote: in the case of an offence under paragraph (d), be liable to a fine of not less than ten thousand ringgit and not more than fifty thousand ringgit for each person harboured
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.56(1)(d),(bb)

claim: Attempting, preparing or abetting any offence under the Immigration Act carries the same punishment as the offence itself (s.56(1A))
quote: shall be guilty of such offence and be liable to the punishment provided for such offence.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.56(1A)

claim: Any offence under the Immigration Act with no special penalty: fine up to RM10,000 or up to 5 years in prison or both (s.57)
quote: Any person guilty of an offence against this Act for which no special penalty is provided shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to both.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.57

claim: The Immigration Act contains no provision on refugees or asylum: the words 'refugee' and 'asylum' do not appear in the Act; every non-citizen needs a valid Entry Permit or Pass, or an exemption order under s.55, to enter (s.6(1))
quote: No person other than a citizen shall enter Malaysia unless
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); the AGC file immigration-act-155-en is only the 1975 revised text; s.6(1). Searched the full 2006 reprint text for 'refugee' and 'asylum': 0 matches (also 0 in the Federal Constitution reprint as at 30 Nov 2025). Absence of a provision cannot be quoted; quote shows the general rule

claim: Any non-citizen unlawfully entering, re-entering or remaining in Malaysia is liable to removal by order of the Director General, whether or not they are prosecuted (s.56(2))
quote: unlawfully remaining in Malaysia shall whether or not any proceedings are taken against him in respect of the offence be liable to be removed from Malaysia by order of the Director General.
note: Immigration Act 1959/63 reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 Jan 2006 (IMI copy); s.56(2)

claim: The AGC Laws of Malaysia English file of the Immigration Act (Act 155) is the 1975 revised text (revised up to 31 Dec 1974, in force 1 May 1975, gazetted 10 Apr 1975), a scanned copy with handwritten amendment marks; it has no ss.55A-55E and does not show current penalties, so it must not be cited for current penalties
quote: Revised up to ... 31st December, 1974 / Date appointed for coming into force ... 1st May, 1975 / Date of publication in Gazette ... 10th April, 1975
note: image-only PDF (CamScanner, no text layer); quote transcribed from rendered page image, p.2; arrangement of sections pp.4-5 lists ss.54-57 with no 55A-55E; p.11 shows s.6(3) with handwritten amendment refs A719, A1154/02

claim: The Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846) amends the Penal Code, Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Arms Act, Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act, Kidnapping Act, Strategic Trade Act and Criminal Procedure Code to abolish the mandatory death penalty and replace imprisonment for natural life and whipping terms
quote: the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, the Strategic Trade Act 2010 and the Criminal Procedure Code in order to abolish the mandatory death penalty, to vary the sentence relating to imprisonment for natural life and whipping
note: Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), Royal Assent 9 June 2023, gazetted 16 June 2023 (as enacted; commencement date not shown in the file); long title

claim: Act 846 comes into operation on a date appointed by the Minister by notification in the Gazette (the date is not in the Act itself)
quote: This Act comes into operation on a date to be appointed by the Minister by notification in the Gazette.
note: Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), Royal Assent 9 June 2023, gazetted 16 June 2023 (as enacted; commencement date not shown in the file); s.1(2). Need to know: the commencement notification (P.U.(B)) date

claim: Drug trafficking (Dangerous Drugs Act s.39B): Act 846 does not remove death from s.39B(2); it lowers the minimum whipping for those not sentenced to death from 15 to 12 strokes and deletes subsections (2A) and (2B)
quote: is amended in section 39b-- (a) in subsection (2), by substituting for the words "be punished with whipping of not less than fifteen strokes" the words "be punished with whipping of not less than twelve strokes"; and (b) by deleting subsections (2a) and (2b).
note: Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), Royal Assent 9 June 2023, gazetted 16 June 2023 (as enacted; commencement date not shown in the file); s.54. The full current wording of DDA s.39B(2) (death or the alternative prison term) is not in this file: Need to know from a current Dangerous Drugs Act reprint

claim: Anyone convicted of drug trafficking after Act 846 comes into force is sentenced under the amended s.39B, even if the offence was committed earlier
quote: if a person is convicted by any court for the commission of an offence under section 39b of the principal Act, the person, whether at a trial or on an appeal, shall be sentenced in accordance with the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act even though the offence was committed before the date of coming into operation of this Act.
note: Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), Royal Assent 9 June 2023, gazetted 16 June 2023 (as enacted; commencement date not shown in the file); s.55

claim: Murder (Penal Code s.302): after Act 846 the punishment is death or imprisonment of 30 to 40 years, and if not sentenced to death, at least 12 strokes of whipping
quote: Section 302 of the Code is amended by inserting after the words "with death" the words "or imprisonment for a term of not less than thirty years but not exceeding forty years and if not sentenced to death, shall also be punished with whipping of not less than twelve strokes".
note: Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), Royal Assent 9 June 2023, gazetted 16 June 2023 (as enacted; commencement date not shown in the file); s.34

claim: Act 846 replaces 'imprisonment for natural life' with 30-40 years in several laws, e.g. the Strategic Trade Act and Criminal Procedure Code s.172D
quote: substituting for the words "imprisonment for natural life" the words "imprisonment for a term of not less than thirty years but not exceeding forty years"
note: Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), Royal Assent 9 June 2023, gazetted 16 June 2023 (as enacted; commencement date not shown in the file); ss.56-59, 62

claim: Passports Act s.12(1)(f): having in one's possession, without lawful authority, a passport issued for someone else is an offence, punishable by a fine up to RM10,000 or up to 5 years in prison or both; this applies to anyone, including an employer holding a worker's passport
quote: without lawful authority, has in his possession any passport or internal travel document issued for the use of some person other than himself;
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12(1)(f). The Act does not name employers; 'anyone, including an employer' follows from 'any person'. Whether consent amounts to 'lawful authority' is not defined in the Act

claim: Penalty for all s.12(1) Passports Act offences (forging or possessing a forged passport, impersonation, false statement to get a passport, holding another person's passport, etc.): fine up to RM10,000 or up to 5 years in prison or both
quote: shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to both.
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12(1) penalty

claim: Passports Act s.12(1)(e): a passport holder who lets another person possess their passport, intending or knowing it may be used by someone else, also commits an offence
quote: allows any person to have possession of any passport or internal travel document issued for his use alone, intending or knowing that the passport or internal travel document may be used by any other person;
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12(1)(e)

claim: Passports Act s.12(1)(a): forging, altering or tampering with one's passport or visa, or using or possessing such a forged or altered passport without lawful authority, is an offence
quote: forges, alters or tampers with his passport or internal travel document, or any visa or endorsement thereon, or without lawful authority uses or attempts to use, or has in his possession, any passport or internal travel document which has been so forged, altered or tampered with;
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12(1)(a)

claim: Passports Act s.12(1)(c): knowingly making a false statement or giving a false document to get a passport or visa for oneself is an offence
quote: with intent to obtain for himself a passport, internal travel document, or an endorsement or visa on his passport, knowingly makes any false statement or produces any document which is to his knowledge false in any particular;
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12(1)(c)

claim: Passports Act s.12A: making a false statement or giving a false document to get a passport or visa for another person: fine RM10,000-50,000 and 1-5 years in prison
quote: Any person who with intent to obtain for any other person a passport, internal travel document, or an endorsement or visa on a passport, knowingly makes any false statement or produces any document which to his knowledge is false in any particular shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of not less than ten thousand ringgit but not more than fifty thousand ringgit and imprisonment for a term of not less than one year but not more than five years.
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12A

claim: Passports Act s.12B: making a false document to be used as a passport: fine RM15,000-100,000 and 2-10 years in prison and up to 6 strokes of the rotan
quote: as a passport for the purposes of this Act shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of not less than fifteen thousand ringgit but not more than one hundred thousand ringgit and imprisonment for a term of not less than two years but not more than ten years and with whipping of not more than six strokes of the rotan.
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; s.12B

claim: The Refworld text of the Passports Act is an unofficial consolidation including amendments only up to Act A948 (in force 1 January 1997)
quote: This is the unofficial consolidation.
note: Passports Act 1966 (Act 150), unofficial consolidation on UNHCR Refworld (Refworld date 1 Apr 1966) including amendments up to Act A948 in force 1 Jan 1997; Refworld comments. Need to know: any amendment after 1997 (check a current AGC reprint)
